_wafNote: Florida, Louisiana and Delaware sit behind Cloudflare/WAF and return 403 if hit twice in quick succession. Keep polling.requestDelayMs at or above 1500 and send the configured user agent. Arkansas, Massachusetts and New Hampshire block automated requests entirely - they may still have feeds, but they cannot be verified without a real browser.

medicalExaminers._comment: County medical-examiner open data. See src/sources/medex.mjs for what this is and is not, and docs/ALERT-SOURCES.md for the full survey of what else was checked. These are the only free public sources found that are county-granular, name specific adulterants, and are current within weeks. They are mortality data - a lagging indicator - so severity is capped at 'elevated' and every item states its own lag. Verified working 2026-08-14.

sources.name: The Cook County Medical Examiner
sources._note: The boolean column is `opioids`. `opioid_related` is not a column and errors. $select names only the date and cause columns - the dataset also carries age, race, gender, incident_street, incident_zip, latitude and longitude, and none of it is ever requested.

sources.name: The Allegheny County Medical Examiner
sources._note: Drugs are pre-parsed into combined_od1..10. Plain datastore_search, NOT datastore_search_sql: that endpoint fails in bursts (verified 2026-08-14 - five consecutive runs failed every call, then recovered, while plain search stayed at 200 throughout) and the SQL path needed five calls per run. This is one call for all 7,751 rows. `fields` is a whitelist of the date and the ten drug columns, so age, sex, race and both ZIP columns are never requested - the same discipline $select gives the Socrata sources. Date field is death_date_and_time, not death_date.

sources.name: The Santa Clara County Medical Examiner
sources._note: Fentanyl-involved deaths only, so the denominator is narrower than Cook's and a share here means 'of fentanyl deaths', not 'of overdose deaths'. Same $select discipline: the dataset carries age, race, gender, zip and lat/lon. Every column in this dataset is typed text, dates included, so date literals must be date-only and month bucketing uses substring().

sources.name: The San Diego County Medical Examiner
sources._note: `opioid_related` is a categorical string, not a boolean - the values are Opioid, Opioid-Fentanyl, Non-Opioid, Non-Disclosure. Querying it as `true` or 'Yes' returns zero rows, which is what made this dataset look unusable on first pass. It also has a real `death_date` (calendar_date); the `year`/`quarter` columns are a red herring. Verified 2026-08-14.

medicalExaminers._lagNote: maxLagDays is measured from the last COMPLETE month, not the newest record - see completeThrough() in src/sources/medex.mjs. Allegheny's newest record is about 2 months old but it is still filling in cases from 4 months back, so its honest anchor is roughly 6 months and 150 would have silently dropped it. Every item states its own lag in the body text.
medicalExaminers._statsNote: maxP is a Fisher exact one-sided p-value, replacing a z-test that treated the estimated baseline as a known rate and inflated the false-alarm rate 2.7x. 0.001 per test budgets roughly a quarter of one false alert per year across 11 substances x 4 counties x ~4 independent windows. See the header above exactP() in src/sources/medex.mjs.
medicalExaminers._denominatorNote: Cook and San Diego count opioid-involved deaths; Allegheny counts all accidental overdose deaths; Santa Clara counts fentanyl-involved deaths. Each alert states its own denominator in the body text, because a share means a different thing under each. WIDENING COOK AND SAN DIEGO WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED ON THE DATA (2026-08-14): the deaths their filters exclude are 382 and 315 respectively over 455 days - about 30% more denominator - and searching those excluded deaths for every watchlist substance found FOUR records in total (2 bromazolam in Cook, 1 xylazine and 1 nitazene in San Diego). Widening would have diluted every share that currently works, and cost statistical power at counts already small enough for minCount to bind, to recover four records nationally. The substances the widening was meant to expose - levamisole and BTMPS - are absent from all four sources including the unfiltered one; see the note above the watchlist in src/sources/medex.mjs.

_evidenceNote: Every source carries an evidence class - lab, official, community - read by src/evidence.mjs. Aggregators (googleNews, gdelt) deliberately have none: they are carriers, and their items are graded by the originator NAMED IN THE TEXT, or dropped if nobody is. The classes gate severity (community and unconfirmed media never publish critical) and set per-class confidence floors. See the header of src/evidence.mjs for why grading the originator rather than the carrier is the load-bearing idea.
